hints: At $x = 1$, $y = 2$, tangent gradient is $3 \implies$ normal gradient $-\frac{1}{3}$.
walkthrough:
Evaluate the curve point and tangent gradient at $x = 1$:
$$y_1 = \frac{4}{5 - 3(1)} = \frac{4}{2} = 2$$
$$m_T = \left.\frac{dy}{dx}\right|_{x=1} = \frac{12}{(5 - 3(1))^2} = \frac{12}{2^2} = 3$$
$$m_N = -\frac{1}{m_T} = -\frac{1}{3}$$

Write the equation of the normal line at $(1, 2)$:
$$y - 2 = -\frac{1}{3}(x - 1) \implies y = -\frac{1}{3}x + \frac{1}{3} + 2 \implies y = -\frac{1}{3}x + \frac{7}{3}$$

Set up the volume of revolution integral for the region bounded by $x = 0$ to $x = 1$:
$$V = \pi \int_0^1 y^2\,dx = \pi \int_0^1 \left(\frac{4}{5 - 3x}\right)^2 dx = 16\pi \int_0^1 (5 - 3x)^{-2}\,dx$$

Integrate using the reverse chain rule:
$$V = 16\pi \left[ \frac{(5 - 3x)^{-1}}{(-1)(-3)} \right]_0^1 = \frac{16\pi}{3} \left[ \frac{1}{5 - 3x} \right]_0^1$$
